html:
The Burundian Civil War was fought from 1993 to 2005 between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebel groups, and killed about 300,000 people.

It began with the murder of President Melchior Ndadaye in October 1993. Hutu rebel movements fought from the hills and from camps in Zaire and Tanzania, while the army cleared Hutu areas, and Pierre Buyoya returned to power in a coup in 1996.

Peace talks led by Julius Nyerere and then Nelson Mandela produced the Arusha Accords of 2000. The largest rebel group, led by Pierre Nkurunziza, made peace in 2003, and he became president after elections in 2005.
sum: The Burundian Civil War was fought from 1993 to 2005 between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebel groups, and killed about 300,000 people.
